rules: HM Land Registry describes INSPIRE Index Polygons as an open-source dataset created for INSPIRE compliance.
INSPIRE Index Polygons contain locations of registered freehold property in England and Wales.
INSPIRE is a subset of HM Land Registry's wider Index Polygons database.
INSPIRE files are divided by local-authority area.
A polygon on a local-authority boundary can appear in both authority files.
INSPIRE polygons show position and indicative extent rather than definitive legal extent.
Every INSPIRE polygon has its own Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
A Land Registry-INSPIRE ID relates to a registered title.
HM Land Registry directs users to Find a Property using the INSPIRE ID to obtain registration and title-plan information.
The registered-title extent cannot be established from INSPIRE polygons alone.
The individual title plan is required to identify the registered-title extent.
One registered title has a single title number but can contain multiple separate polygons.
Each separate polygon under a title has a separate Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
Absence of an INSPIRE ID can indicate unregistered land, leasehold registration or another tenure excluded from INSPIRE.
HM Land Registry directs users to the index map to check whether land is registered.
INSPIRE reuse is governed by the Open Government Licence.
INSPIRE reuse requires HM Land Registry attribution.
Reuse of INSPIRE polygon geometry also requires Ordnance Survey attribution.
The current INSPIRE dataset is updated on the first Sunday of each month.
Each monthly INSPIRE release represents data from the previous month.
The current download index states publication on 5 July 2026.
The July 2026 download index lists London Borough of Barnet.
The July 2026 download index lists London Borough of Enfield.
HM Land Registry supplies INSPIRE files as GML and states that GIS software is required to view them.
HM Land Registry captures polygon geometry against British National Grid.
HM Land Registry identifies British National Grid as EPSG:27700 in its GML guidance.
HM Land Registry warns that BNG-to-WGS84 reprojection can move some features by up to 15 metres.
The National Polygon Service is a separate licensed chargeable service containing National Polygon, Title Descriptor and Title Number/UPRN Look Up datasets.
The National Polygon dataset includes both freehold and leasehold titles, unlike the freehold-focused INSPIRE subset.
HM Land Registry's catalogue describes INSPIRE as free monthly GML with no API, so the paid National Polygon Service must not be silently substituted as the free public source.
The current Planning Data documentation exposes more than 100 planning and housing datasets through a common API.
Coordinate queries accept latitude and longitude and return entities whose geometry intersects the point.
Multiple dataset parameters can be supplied in a single coordinate query.
Planning Data documents UPRN or postcode search through the q parameter.
Planning Data states that UPRN search is more precise than coordinate search for registered properties.
Raw spatial searches accept Well-Known Text geometry.
Planning Data says raw spatial-query coordinates should use WGS84 EPSG:4326.
geometry_relation supports within for spatial filtering.
geometry_relation supports intersects for spatial filtering.
geometry_relation supports contains for spatial filtering.
geometry_relation supports covers and coveredby for spatial filtering.
geometry_relation supports touches, equals, disjoint, overlaps and crosses.
geometry_entity allows a stored entity geometry to be reused as a spatial filter.
offset pagination is documented for large result sets.
Planning Data responses expose next, previous, first and last pagination links.
The field parameter can restrict returned fields.
exclude_field can remove fields from responses and is subordinate to field when both are supplied.
The quality parameter can filter entity results.
Planning Data documents that portfolio screening has no batch endpoint.
Planning Data recommends polite rate limiting when sending repeated per-property requests.
For large portfolios Planning Data recommends bulk downloads plus local spatial intersections.
Bulk downloads are available in CSV and JSON and, where applicable, GeoJSON and Parquet.
The listed-building specification accepts CSV, GeoJSON, GML and GeoPackage.
Listed-building data can be uploaded at a stable URL or served through OGC WFS or ArcGIS API.
Listed-building geometry is specified as polygon or multipolygon in WGS84.
CSV geometry for listed buildings is represented as Well-Known Text.
Listed-building references must be unique within the dataset and permanent across updates.
Listed-building records use Historic England List Entry Number as the listed-building identifier.
An active listed-building record leaves end-date blank; a delisted record records the date the designation ceased.

The live listed-building dataset page states that its point data does not define the legal extent of the area affected by listing, so point-only matches cannot substitute for authoritative boundary geometry.
The Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 1m is a raster terrain model covering about 99 percent of England at 1m resolution.
The DTM is produced from the last or only laser return.
Surface objects are removed from the DSM using bespoke algorithms and manual editing.
The current 1m composite was produced in 2022.
The 1m composite combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist the composite uses the newest best-resolution data.
Resampled source data is merged after bilinear interpolation.
The 2022 composite contains surveys undertaken between 6 June 2000 and 2 April 2022.
The DTM 1m coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The 1m record exposes WMS, WCS, WMTS and OGC API service links.
Environment Agency guidance distinguishes WMS summarised imagery from WCS raw elevation pixels.
The persistent LIDAR Composite WCS scheme is designed to remain stable across future updates.
The supported raw elevation service is OGC WCS 2.0.1.
WCS NoData pixels must not be treated as terrain elevations.
The 1m composite metadata identifier is 13787b9a-26a4-4775-8523-806d13af58fc.
The Time Stamped DTM archive contains site-specific surveys dating back to 1998.
Time Stamped DTM data exists at 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m resolutions depending on the survey.
Time Stamped DTM downloads are GeoTIFF rasters in 5km zip files.
Time Stamped DTM elevations are expressed in metres relative to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
Time Stamped DTM data is aligned to the OS Grid.
Time Stamped metadata identifies survey dates, resolution, transformation and geoidal model used at a location.
The DTM 2m composite is a separate product with the same broad survey period and EPSG:27700 CRS.
The DTM 10m composite is resampled from the DTM 2m product using bilinear interpolation.
The DTM 10m product is supplied as a single GeoTIFF aligned to the OS National Grid.
The DTM 10m record states annual update frequency and Open Government Licence use.
The retired 25cm composite product is no longer available and was replaced by the 1m composite.
The Environment Agency directs users to the survey download service for the 1m composite and archived 25cm time-stamped data.
Source LIDAR surveys used in the composites have stated vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15cm RMSE.
Vertical RMSE is a dataset accuracy statistic and must not be promoted as a candidate-point elevation.
Survey-index metadata must be used to determine which source survey contributes at a candidate location before assigning survey provenance.
OS Terrain 50 is an Open Data digital terrain model for Great Britain.
The product is designed for broad landscape analysis at lower resolution than OS Terrain 5.
OS Terrain 50 is updated annually in July.
Current OS documentation states that the product is free to view, download and use for commercial, educational and personal purposes.
Terrain 50 grid and contour products are created from the same underlying source data.
Both grid and contour forms use 10km by 10km geographic tiles.
Tile identifiers use the National Grid reference of the tile's south-west corner.
The grid is a regular set of heighted points at 50m post spacing.
The contour product uses 10m interval standard contours.
The contour product includes mean high water and mean low water boundaries and spot heights.
Terrain 50 grid data is available in ASCII grid and GML 3.2.1.
Terrain 50 contour data is available in GML 3.2.1, Esri Shapefile, GeoPackage and vector tiles.
ASCII grid heights are calculated at the centre of each pixel.
ASCII rows are ordered west to east.
Each ASCII grid row contains 200 pixels.
Each pixel is 50m by 50m.
Grid height values are supplied to the nearest 0.1m.
Grid tile supply includes ASC, GML, PRJ, ASC.AUX.XML and per-tile metadata XML files.
OS Terrain 50 per-tile metadata follows the GEMINI metadata standard.
Per-tile metadata identifies the 10km National Grid tile reference.
OS Terrain 50 uses British National Grid as the horizontal reference and Ordnance Datum Newlyn for heights.
The product is supplied online with no registration required.
The tiled national dataset contains 2,858 10km tiles arranged in 55 100km grid-square folders.
The full national grid supply is about 157 MB compressed.
Ordnance Survey recommends download-manager tooling for managing the tiled product.
Terrain 50 is maintained by full annual tile resupply.
The product overview states that Terrain 50 grid data has been verified to 4m RMSE.
The 4m RMSE value is a product accuracy statistic and cannot be substituted for a candidate-point height.
The current OS known-data-issues page states there are no live known issues for Terrain 50 at present.
Terrain 50 is supplied as inert data without manipulation software, so extraction and cell addressing must be implemented and validated separately.

Exact Planning Data result binding for parcel refs 52040420, 52213916 and 52213412 remains absent.
